CONTEXT OF THE JOB:
The Alfred Lerner College of Business and Economics at the
University of Delaware invites applications for the position of
inaugural Executive Director of The Siegfried Institute for
Leadership and Free Enterprise. We seek a visionary leader to
establish and lead this new Institute. The Executive Director will
report to the Dean of the Alfred Lerner College of Business and
Economics.
The University of Delaware’s business school, the Alfred Lerner
College of Business and Economics, is a hub for innovation,
business and economics research and career success. With hands-on
experiences and a technology-driven curriculum, Lerner equips
students to navigate the evolving business world and drive change
worldwide.
The mission of the Siegfried Institute is to research and teach
the capabilities and characteristics of effective Leadership, while
further studying the critical role that the basic principles of
Limited Government, Rule of Law, and Free Enterprise play in
supporting Individual Freedom and developing effective Individual
Leadership. These basic principles are pivotal to conservative
economics and align with the foundational values of the United
States. Through its focus on the U.S. Constitutional framework, the
Siegfried Institute will further seek to enrich the lives of
individuals, their families, and their communities, as well as
benefit our national interest.
Conservative economics, exemplified by the work of 18th-century
economist Adam Smith, and Nobel Prize winners Friedrich Hayek and
Milton Friedman, embrace free-market capitalism and challenge the
Keynesian school of thought, which supports stronger government
involvement in the economy. Within the continuum of economic
theory, the Siegfried Institute will explore how the governmental
environment, including regulations and taxes, affects individual
freedom, authority, responsibility, and motivation.
This new Institute will facilitate dialogue between different
schools of thought and contribute to scholarly and public discourse
on economic policies, while at the same time providing a forum for
business leaders, academics, and others interested in these topics.
Examples of activities for serving the Institute’s mission include
annual conference/symposia, invited lecture series, periodic
webinars, scholarly publications and white papers, fellowships, and
workshops. Such engagement will make the Institute a producer of
visionary leaders and a national and international thought leader
in Leadership and economic policies that best support and drive
effective Leadership and Free Enterprise.
MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

As the inaugural Executive Director of the Institute, build a
solid organizational foundation for the Institute’s long
term-success.
Develop organizational strategies in consultation with key
internal and external stakeholders to implement the Institute’s
mission and objectives.
Lead, manage, develop, and mentor the Institute’s staff,
including professional and administrative personnel.
In partnership with Lerner College and UD’s Development and
Alumni Relations Officers, establish fundraising goals and
strategies for the Institute, and develop and execute fundraising
strategies. Seek and secure sponsorships and co-sponsorships for
Institute initiatives and programs.
Raise the Institute’s national profile within and beyond UD.
Utilize both traditional and social media channels to communicate
regarding Institute activities within the UD guidelines. With
support from UD and Lerner’s Public Affairs staff, manage the
Institute’s public relations.
Work to establish and maintain the Institute’s Advisory Board
to seek advice and support and periodically reassess and, where
necessary, revise the Institute’s Strategic Plan and other
Institute initiatives.
In consultation with the Lerner Dean’s Office, develop and/or
implement effective strategic risk management processes.
Develop and manage the Institute’s budget and all fiscal
matters consistent with University policies and the Institute’s
endowment and gift requirements.
Ensure effective records management.
Model leadership principles as an active and engaged member of
the Lerner College of Business and Economics and the greater
University of Delaware community.
Engage with other University of Delaware and Lerner Centers and
academic units to identify potential scholarly publication topics
relevant to the Institute’s mission and to develop and promote
engaging activities that support innovative scholarly work.
Contribute to public discourse on policies related to the
Institute’s mission.
Conceptualize, develop, and implement programs that will
provide a forum for students, business leaders, academics, and
others interested in economic policies.
Author articles or postings regarding emerging topics for
publication in periodicals, blogs, social media, media, or other
channels.
Participate in conferences within and beyond UD programs and
projects as a speaker, commentator, moderator, panelist, or
lecturer.
Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Advanced degree in Business, Economics, Law, or a related field
preferred. Candidates with substantial relevant business or
professional experience will also be considered.
Demonstrated high level of accomplishment and thought
leadership in the areas of leadership and free enterprise.
Demonstrated knowledge of and intellectual engagement with
conservative economics and the broader principles described in the
mission statement above.
Exemplary and unquestionable integrity.
Ability and willingness to collaborate with units across
campus.
Experience successfully managing and developing staff and
leading an organization.
Proven success in leading organizations through the effective
implementation of strategy and tactics, delivering measurable
results that meet or exceed organizational objectives.
Ability to build consensus, foster collaboration, and lead in
an inclusive and supportive manner.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
